statement: Which of the following describes the mechanism by which low-dose aspirin can lead to an increase in serum uric acid concentrations, potentially worsening a gouty condition?
options: Direct stimulation of purine synthesis from hypoxanthine
Irreversible binding to the uricase enzyme
Competition with uric acid for the secretion mechanism in the proximal tubule
Promotion of urate crystal phagocytosis by macrophages
Inhibition of the xanthine oxidase enzyme in the liver
correctOption: Competition with uric acid for the secretion mechanism in the proximal tubule
optionExplanations: Aspirin does not stimulate purine synthesis. It affects the elimination phase of uric acid rather than the production phase.
Humans lack the uricase enzyme naturally (which is why pegloticase is used). Aspirin does not interact with this recombinant enzyme in a way that raises urate.
Aspirin is a weak acid. In the proximal tubule, it competes with the active secretion of uric acid into the lumen, leading to decreased excretion and higher serum levels.
Aspirin, as an NSAID, would actually inhibit inflammatory processes; however, its renal effect on urate secretion outweighs its anti-inflammatory benefit in the context of gout.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase; aspirin has no inhibitory effect on this enzyme and does not reduce the production of uric acid.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 316 (Book Page): Elevation of uric acid levels by this mechanism occurs with aspirin (another weak acid) over much of its dose range. [Mechanism: compete with uric acid for secretion by the tubule]

category: Describe the pharmacological significance of Redman Syndrome
statement: A physician requires a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) for a postoperative patient who is unable to take medications orally. Which of the following is the only NSAID available in a parenteral formulation for this use?
options: Celecoxib
Ketorolac
Indomethacin
Naproxen
Ibuprofen
correctOption: Ketorolac
optionExplanations: Celecoxib is a COX-2 selective inhibitor available for oral use; it is not available in a parenteral form according to the provided text.
Ketorolac is specifically highlighted as the only NSAID available for systemic parenteral (IV or IM) use, making it ideal for post-surgical pain management.
While indomethacin is used for acute gout and closing a patent ductus arteriosus, the text identifies ketorolac as the unique parenteral analgesic in this class.
Naproxen is noteworthy for its longer half-life permitting less frequent dosing, but it is administered orally, not parenterally.
Ibuprofen is well absorbed orally and has a short half-life, but the text specifies it is not the unique parenteral agent mentioned.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 314 (Book Page): Ketorolac is notable... It is the only NSAID available in a parenteral formulation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Which of the following biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) is specifically classified as an anti-interleukin-6 (IL-6) agent?
options: Tocilizumab
Anakinra
Abatacept
Golimumab
Rituximab
correctOption: Tocilizumab
optionExplanations: Tocilizumab is the prototype anti-IL-6 receptor antibody used in rheumatoid arthritis to reduce systemic inflammation.
Anakinra is an interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist, belonging to the anti-IL-1 subclass.
Abatacept is classified as a T-cell modulator, not an anti-IL-6 agent.
Golimumab is an anti-TNF-alpha biological agent, categorized with infliximab and etanercept.
Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody targeting B lymphocytes (CD20), not interleukin-6.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Anti-IL-6 drugs (tocilizumab) Upper respiratory tract infections, headache, hypertension, and elevated liver enzymes

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: What is the primary mechanism by which the recombinant enzyme pegloticase reduces serum urate levels in patients with refractory chronic gout?
options: Antagonism of the interleukin-1 receptor
Inhibition of microtubule assembly in synoviocytes
Irreversible inhibition of xanthine oxidase
Conversion of uric acid to the soluble metabolite allantoin
Competitive inhibition of the URAT1 transporter
correctOption: Conversion of uric acid to the soluble metabolite allantoin
optionExplanations: Anakinra and canakinumab are IL-1 inhibitors; pegloticase is an enzyme therapy for urate lowering.
This is the mechanism of colchicine, which reduces leukocyte migration rather than lowering urate levels.
Allopurinol and febuxostat inhibit xanthine oxidase; pegloticase is a uricase enzyme that breaks down uric acid directly.
Humans lack uricase; pegloticase provides this enzyme to convert insoluble uric acid into highly soluble allantoin for renal excretion.
Uricosurics like probenecid inhibit transporters; pegloticase works through metabolic conversion.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase. This enzyme, absent in humans, converts uric acid to the soluble allantoin, which can be eliminated by the kidney.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the therapeutic hierarchy of rheumatoid arthritis, how are corticosteroids classified regarding their rate of action compared to other agents?
options: Slow acting, requiring 6 weeks to 6 months for any benefit
Permanent modifiers, causing the reversal of joint destruction
Short acting, requiring hourly administration for efficacy
Intermediate acting, slower than NSAIDs but faster than other DMARDs
Rapid acting, with clinical benefits appearing faster than NSAIDs
correctOption: Intermediate acting, slower than NSAIDs but faster than other DMARDs
optionExplanations: This describes conventional DMARDs (Slow-acting antirheumatic drugs), not corticosteroids.
Unlike DMARDs, corticosteroids are generally used for symptom control and are too toxic for routine chronic use as modifiers.
Corticosteroids are typically administered daily or on a tapered schedule, not hourly.
Corticosteroids bridge the gap between rapid NSAIDs and slow-acting DMARDs like methotrexate, which take weeks to months.
NSAIDs provide the most rapid relief of symptoms; corticosteroids are slower than NSAIDs.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Corticosteroids can be considered anti-inflammatory drugs with an intermediate rate of action (ie, slower than NSAIDs but faster than other DMARDs).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 32-year-old female with severe rheumatoid arthritis is being treated with a drug that interferes with T-lymphocyte activity. She presents with elevated liver enzymes and expresses a desire to conceive. Which of the following drugs is most likely associated with both hepatotoxicity and significant teratogenic risk?
options: Anakinra
Etanercept
Hydroxychloroquine
Leflunomide
Sulfasalazine
correctOption: Leflunomide
optionExplanations: Anakinra is an IL-1 antagonist with a toxicity profile focused on infection and injection-site reactions.
Etanercept is a TNF-alpha blocker; while it increases infection risk, it is not classified as a primary hepatotoxic teratogen like leflunomide.
Hydroxychloroquine is primarily associated with ocular toxicity and rash, not significant teratogenicity.
Leflunomide is a potent DMARD that interferes with T-cells and is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to high teratogenic risk and potential hepatotoxicity.
Sulfasalazine commonly causes GI disturbance and leukopenia, but is not the primary teratogen in this class.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Table 36-2 Leflunomide Teratogen, hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal disturbance, skin reactions

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: When contrasting xanthine oxidase inhibitors used for chronic gout, which characteristic is unique to febuxostat compared to allopurinol?
options: It significantly increases the production of less soluble xanthines
It is an irreversible suicide inhibitor of the enzyme
It is used primarily as an adjunct to cancer chemotherapy
It requires metabolic activation by xanthine oxidase to function
It is a nonpurine inhibitor with higher selectivity
correctOption: It is a nonpurine inhibitor with higher selectivity
optionExplanations: Febuxostat increases hypoxanthine and xanthine concentrations, but these are more soluble than uric acid, reducing crystal formation.
Allopurinol is converted to alloxanthine, which is the irreversible suicide inhibitor; febuxostat is a reversible inhibitor.
Allopurinol is typically used for tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis; febuxostat is mainly for chronic gout.
Allopurinol is a prodrug activated by xanthine oxidase; febuxostat does not require this activation.
Febuxostat's nonpurine structure allows it to selectively target xanthine oxidase without affecting other purine/pyrimidine metabolic enzymes.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): The newer drug febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase that is more selective than allopurinol and alloxanthine, which inhibit other enzymes involved in purine and pyrimidine metabolism.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Which of the following immune cells is the primary target for the monoclonal antibody rituximab when used as a disease-modifying agent in rheumatoid arthritis?
options: Neutrophils
B lymphocytes
T lymphocytes
Macrophages
Monocytes
correctOption: B lymphocytes
optionExplanations: While neutrophils are involved in inflammation (and targeted by colchicine's microtubule inhibition), they are not the target of rituximab.
Rituximab targets the CD20 antigen on the surface of B lymphocytes, leading to their depletion.
Drugs like abatacept, cyclosporine, and leflunomide target T lymphocytes.
Gold compounds are noted to interfere primarily with macrophage activity.
Monocytes are not the primary target of rituximab; it is specific for the B-cell lineage.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Other drugs appear to interfere with the activity of T lymphocytes... B lymphocytes (rituximab), or macrophages (gold compounds).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
coreConcept: Aspirin Effect on Uric Acid Excretion
statement: A patient with a history of under-excretion of uric acid is warned against using certain analgesics for minor pain. Why can aspirin at common doses be detrimental in a patient with gout?
options: It inhibits the gastrointestinal absorption of uricosuric agents
It accelerates the conversion of xanthine to uric acid
It causes rapid precipitation of uric acid crystals in the proximal tubule
It competes with uric acid for renal tubular secretion, potentially elevating serum urate
It irreversibly inhibits the xanthine oxidase enzyme in the liver
correctOption: It competes with uric acid for renal tubular secretion, potentially elevating serum urate
optionExplanations: Aspirin's primary interaction with urate handling occurs at the renal tubule, not in the gastrointestinal tract.
Xanthine oxidase is not influenced by aspirin; its action is limited to prostaglandin pathways.
Aspirin doesn't directly cause precipitation; it reduces the excretion, which increases the total body pool of urate.
As a weak acid, aspirin competes for the secretory transport mechanism in the kidney, which can decrease urate excretion and worsen hyperuricemia.
Aspirin is a COX inhibitor, not a xanthine oxidase inhibitor.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 316 (Book Page): At low doses, these agents may also compete with uric acid for secretion by the tubule and occasionally can elevate, rather than reduce, serum uric acid concentration. Elevation of uric acid levels by this mechanism occurs with aspirin (another weak acid) over much of its dose range.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 67-year-old male with severe rheumatoid arthritis and co-existing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is being evaluated for biological therapy. Which T-cell modulator is associated with a specific risk of COPD exacerbations as a potential toxicity?
options: Tofacitinib
Abatacept
Tocilizumab
Infliximab
Rituximab
correctOption: Abatacept
optionExplanations: Tofacitinib (Janus kinase inhibitor) causes neutropenia and lipid changes, but not COPD-specific issues.
Abatacept, a T-cell costimulation modulator, has been clinically noted to cause exacerbations in patients with pre-existing COPD.
Tocilizumab is associated with upper respiratory infections and liver enzyme elevation, but not specifically highlighted for COPD flares.
Infliximab (anti-TNF) is more famously associated with TB reactivation and lymphoma risk than COPD exacerbation.
Rituximab's main concerns are infusion reactions and infections, not pulmonary disease exacerbation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Table 36-2 Abatacept (T-cell modulator) Infection, exacerbation of COPD, hypersensitivity reactions

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Gold compounds are rarely used today but were historically significant DMARDs. What is the pharmacological basis for their anti-inflammatory action in rheumatoid arthritis?
options: Antagonism of the tumor necrosis factor receptor
Reversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2 in the joints
Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase in immune cells
Blockade of Janus kinase (JAK) signaling pathways
Interference with the activity of macrophages
correctOption: Interference with the activity of macrophages
optionExplanations: Anti-TNF drugs like etanercept act as receptor antagonists or binders; gold is not a biologic antagonist.
NSAIDs like celecoxib inhibit COX-2; gold compounds have a much slower and broader immune-modulating effect.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase; gold compounds do not.
Tofacitinib is the JAK inhibitor; gold compounds pre-date this targeted molecular therapy.
Gold compounds (like auranofin) primarily target and suppress macrophage function to reduce the inflammatory burden in joints.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Other drugs appear to interfere with the activity of T lymphocytes... B lymphocytes... or macrophages (gold compounds).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Which of the following NSAIDs is distinguished by a short half-life of approximately 2 hours and is frequently preferred for its relative safety and low cost among nonselective agents?
options: Indomethacin
Naproxen
Ketorolac
Ibuprofen
Piroxicam
correctOption: Ibuprofen
optionExplanations: Indomethacin is a potent NSAID but is associated with more significant toxicities, including bone marrow suppression and severe GI issues.
Naproxen also has a significantly longer half-life than 2 hours, facilitating twice-daily dosing.
Ketorolac is primarily used as a parenteral analgesic for short-term pain, not as a standard low-cost oral anti-inflammatory agent for long-term safety.
Ibuprofen is the prototype short-acting NSAID with a 2-hour half-life and a favorable safety/cost profile.
Piroxicam has a very long half-life, allowing for once-daily dosing, unlike ibuprofen.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 314 (Book Page): Ibuprofen has a half-life of about 2 h, is relatively safe, and is the least expensive of the older, nonselective NSAIDs.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 62-year-old male with chronic, treatment-refractory tophaceous gout is started on pegloticase. What is the primary biochemical mechanism by which this agent reduces the total body urate pool?
options: Competitive inhibition of the URAT1 transporter in the proximal tubule
Disruption of microtubule polymerization within polynuclear leukocytes
Antagonism of the Interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor on synoviocytes
Irreversible suicide inhibition of the xanthine oxidase enzyme
Conversion of uric acid to the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
correctOption: Conversion of uric acid to the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
optionExplanations: This is the mechanism of uricosuric agents like probenecid and sulfinpyrazone, which increase renal excretion rather than enzymatic conversion.
Microtubule disruption is the mechanism of action for colchicine, which reduces the inflammatory response to crystals but does not lower urate levels.
IL-1 receptor antagonism is the mechanism of anakinra, used to manage inflammation in gout and RA, but it does not affect biochemical urate levels.
This describes the mechanism of allopurinol, which is converted to oxypurinol to inhibit uric acid production, not pegloticase.
Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase that enzymatically converts poorly soluble uric acid into allantoin, which is much more soluble and easily excreted by the kidneys.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): [Pegloticase] This enzyme, absent in humans, converts uric acid to the soluble allantoin, which can be eliminated by the kidney.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: When comparing the xanthine oxidase inhibitors used in chronic gout management, which characteristic distinguishes febuxostat from allopurinol and its active metabolite oxypurinol?
options: It requires metabolic activation by xanthine oxidase to become effective
It predominantly inhibits enzymes involved in pyrimidine metabolism
It is a purine-analog that acts as a suicide substrate for the enzyme
It is a nonpurine inhibitor with higher selectivity for xanthine oxidase
It is less effective than allopurinol in lowering serum uric acid levels
correctOption: It is a nonpurine inhibitor with higher selectivity for xanthine oxidase
optionExplanations: Allopurinol requires conversion to oxypurinol (alloxanthine) by xanthine oxidase to exert its main effect; febuxostat is active in its parent form.
Allopurinol is the one known to inhibit other enzymes in pyrimidine metabolism; febuxostat is more selective and avoids these interactions according to text data.
Allopurinol is a purine analog and a suicide inhibitor; febuxostat is a nonpurine, reversible inhibitor.
Febuxostat is structurally distinct (nonpurine) and exhibits greater selectivity for xanthine oxidase, whereas allopurinol can affect other purine/pyrimidine metabolic pathways.
Clinical trials actually suggest that febuxostat is more effective than allopurinol in lowering serum uric acid concentrations.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): The newer drug febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase that is more selective than allopurinol and alloxanthine, which inhibit other enzymes involved in purine and pyrimidine metabolism.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient with a history of recurrent gout and hypertension is being considered for uricosuric therapy. The physician notes that the patient has a known allergy to sulfonamide-derived diuretics. Which pharmacological property of uricosuric agents necessitates caution in this patient?
options: They inhibit the synthesis of renal prostaglandins needed for vasodilation
They irreversibly bind to the renal proximal tubule transporters
They are weak acids that compete for biliary secretion
They share structural allergenicity with sulfonamide antimicrobials
They induce hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes involved in drug metabolism
correctOption: They share structural allergenicity with sulfonamide antimicrobials
optionExplanations: This is a property of NSAIDs (COX inhibitors), not uricosuric agents like probenecid or sulfinpyrazone.
Binding to transporters in the proximal tubule is competitive and reversible, not irreversible.
Uricosurics are weak acids, but they compete for renal tubular reabsorption and secretion, not primarily biliary secretion.
Probenecid and sulfinpyrazone are sulfonamide derivatives; therefore, patients with hypersensitivity to other sulfonamides (like thiazides or sulfamethoxazole) are at risk for cross-reactions.
Uricosurics do not typically act as significant hepatic enzyme inducers; their primary drug interactions involve competition for renal tubular transporters.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Because they are sulfonamides, the uricosuric drugs may share allergenicity with other classes of sulfonamide drugs (diuretics, antimicrobials, oral hypoglycemic drugs).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 7-year-old boy with severe growth failure is diagnosed with a deficiency in insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) that is unresponsive to exogenous growth hormone (GH) therapy. He is prescribed mecasermin. Which clinical instruction is most critical to prevent the primary toxicity associated with this treatment?
options: Administer the drug exclusively at bedtime to avoid orthostatic hypotension
Monitor for symptoms of hypernatremia and polyuria daily
Avoid protein-rich foods to prevent renal stones and hypercalciuria
Consume a meal or snack shortly before the administration of the drug
Restrict fluid intake to prevent symptomatic peripheral edema
correctOption: Consume a meal or snack shortly before the administration of the drug
optionExplanations: Mecasermin is not associated with orthostatic hypotension in the provided text; its primary concern is metabolic (glucose levels).
Hypernatremia and polyuria are characteristic of diabetes insipidus (treated with vasopressin), not mecasermin therapy.
Mecasermin is used for growth failure; protein restriction would be counterproductive to the goal of growth and is not a strategy to mitigate its toxicity.
Mecasermin is recombinant human IGF-1. Like insulin, IGF-1 has glucose-lowering effects; therefore, hypoglycemia is the most significant side effect, necessitating food intake before dosing.
While GH can cause edema, mecasermin's most critical and acute toxicity listed in the text is hypoglycemia.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 323 (Book Page): Its most important toxicity is hypoglycemia, which can be prevented by consumption of a snack or meal shortly before mecasermin administration.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of rheumatoid arthritis, various DMARDs target specific cell populations or signaling molecules. Which of the following agents is correctly matched with its primary cellular or molecular target?
options: Gold compounds: Selective depletion of T-helper lymphocytes
Leflunomide: Antagonism of the Interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor
Rituximab: Interference with the activity of B lymphocytes
Sulfasalazine: Inhibition of Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) receptors
Abatacept: Direct inhibition of Janus Kinase 1 (JAK1)
correctOption: Rituximab: Interference with the activity of B lymphocytes
optionExplanations: Gold compounds are described in the text as interfering primarily with the activity of macrophages, not selective T-helper depletion.
Tocilizumab targets the IL-6 receptor; Leflunomide is noted for interfering with T lymphocyte activity (and inhibiting pyrimidine synthesis).
Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody that targets B lymphocytes, preventing their contribution to the autoimmune inflammatory process in RA.
Sulfasalazine is listed as a drug that interferes with T lymphocyte activity, while anti-TNF drugs (like infliximab) target TNF-alpha specifically.
Tofacitinib is the Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor; Abatacept is described as a T-cell modulator.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Other drugs appear to interfere with the activity of T lymphocytes (eg, sulfasalazine, hydroxychloroquine, cyclosporine, leflunomide... ), B lymphocytes ( rituximab ), or macrophages (gold compounds).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 5-year-old girl with a high-grade fever and a varicella-like rash is given a salicylate-containing medication for symptomatic relief. She subsequently develops rapid-onset encephalopathy and liver degeneration. What is the most likely diagnosis associated with this drug-viral interaction?
options: Cushing's Syndrome
Reye's Syndrome
Sjögren’s Syndrome
Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
Fanconi Syndrome
correctOption: Reye's Syndrome
optionExplanations: Cushing's Syndrome results from excess glucocorticoids, presenting with weight gain and striae, not acute liver failure.
Reye's Syndrome is the classic association with aspirin use in children during viral infections (like varicella or influenza), leading to hepatic and brain damage.
Sjögren’s Syndrome is an autoimmune disorder affecting moisture-producing glands, not an acute pediatric drug-viral reaction.
Stevens-Johnson Syndrome is a severe skin reaction often drug-induced but is not characterized primarily by liver degeneration and encephalopathy.
Fanconi Syndrome is a renal tubule disorder and is not associated with the acute hepatic/encephalopathy triad seen in Reye's Syndrome.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 314 (Book Page): Children with viral infections who are treated with aspirin have an increased risk for developing Reye’s syndrome, a rare but serious syndrome of rapid liver degeneration and encephalopathy.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 45-year-old male with acromegaly is treated with octreotide. During follow-up, he complains of right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals. Ultrasonography confirms the presence of cholelithiasis. What is the mechanism behind this specific adverse effect?
options: Induction of hypertriglyceridemia and LDL elevation
Direct cytotoxicity to the biliary ductal epithelium
Inhibition of cholecystokinin release and gallbladder contractility
Competitive antagonism of hepatic LDL receptors
Systemic dehydration leading to concentrated bile salts
correctOption: Inhibition of cholecystokinin release and gallbladder contractility
optionExplanations: Tofacitinib increases LDL/HDL, but octreotide is not typically associated with this as the cause of gallstones.
The drug causes stones via functional inhibition of gallbladder motility rather than direct ductal toxicity.

Octreotide is a somatostatin analog; somatostatin inhibits the release of many gastrointestinal hormones, including those like CCK that stimulate gallbladder contraction, leading to bile stasis and stone formation.
Octreotide does not work through LDL receptor antagonism.
While high-dose aspirin can cause dehydration, octreotide-induced gallstones are a result of inhibited hormonal signaling for gallbladder emptying.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 324 (Book Page): Octreotide and lanreotide cause significant gastrointestinal disturbances, gallstones, and cardiac conduction abnormalities.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 50-year-old patient with progressive rheumatoid arthritis is started on tofacitinib after failing methotrexate. Routine laboratory monitoring shows an increase in both LDL and HDL cholesterol levels. Based on its classification and mechanism, which of the following is an additional monitoring requirement for this specific drug?
options: Monitoring for neutropenia, anemia, and infection risk
Urinalysis for heavy proteinuria and hematuria
Serial ophthalmic exams for retinal toxicity
Frequent dental exams for mucosal ulcers and gingival hyperplasia
Bleeding time monitoring due to irreversible COX inhibition
correctOption: Monitoring for neutropenia, anemia, and infection risk
optionExplanations: Tofacitinib inhibits JAK signaling, which is involved in hematopoiesis and immune function; thus, it can cause neutropenia, anemia, and increase the risk of infections.
Proteinuria is associated with penicillamine and gold compounds, not primarily with tofacitinib.
Retinal toxicity is a classic side effect of hydroxychloroquine, not Janus kinase inhibitors like tofacitinib.
While methotrexate can cause mucosal ulcers, the specific toxicity profile for tofacitinib highlighted includes hematologic and lipid changes.
Irreversible COX inhibition and bleeding time concerns are specific to aspirin, whereas tofacitinib is a kinase inhibitor.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Tofacitinib (Janus kinase inhibitor) [Toxicity:] Infection, neutropenia, anemia, and increases in LDL and HDL

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of chronic gout, why is it recommended to wait 1–2 weeks after the resolution of an acute attack before initiating a xanthine oxidase inhibitor or a uricosuric agent?
options: To ensure that any residual indomethacin has been completely cleared
To allow the renal tubules to recover from urate-induced necrosis
Because these drugs are only absorbed when serum urate is below 6 mg/dL
To prevent the precipitation of a new acute attack due to rapid urate shifts
To allow the liver to regenerate xanthine oxidase enzymes
correctOption: To prevent the precipitation of a new acute attack due to rapid urate shifts
optionExplanations: Indomethacin clearance is fast (NSAID half-lives are short, Page 314); the 2-week delay is a physiological precaution regarding joint inflammation.
The delay is not due to renal necrosis recovery; it is related to the dynamics of uric acid crystals in the joints.
Drug absorption is independent of the serum urate level; the concern is the inflammatory response to fluctuating levels.
Rapid changes in serum uric acid levels (either up or down) can trigger the mobilization of urate from tissue stores, precipitating a flare-up of acute gouty arthritis.
Xanthine oxidase inhibitors do not destroy the enzyme in the liver in a way that requires regeneration before starting therapy; they inhibit the active enzyme.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Like uricosuric agents, these drugs are usually withheld for 1–2 weeks after an acute episode of gouty arthritis ... to avoid an acute attack.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient is prescribed a DMARD that is specifically noted for its potential to cause teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity. It is classified as a drug that interferes with T lymphocyte activity. Which drug fits this description?
options: Sulfasalazine
Hydroxychloroquine
Anakinra
Leflunomide
Abatacept
correctOption: Leflunomide
optionExplanations: Sulfasalazine toxicities include leukopenia and rash, but it is not the primary drug associated with high-risk teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity in this group.
Hydroxychloroquine is noted for ocular toxicity and myopathy, not primarily as a major teratogen in this context.
Anakinra is an IL-1 receptor antagonist, not a drug that directly interferes with T lymphocyte activity as its primary mechanism listed.
Leflunomide is a T-cell modulator DMARD that is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity and requires liver function monitoring.
Abatacept is a T-cell modulator but its listed toxicities are infection and COPD exacerbation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Table 36-2: Leflunomide [Toxicity:] Teratogen, hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal disturbance, skin reactions. ... Other drugs appear to interfere with the activity of T lymphocytes (eg, ... leflunomide).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 42-year-old female patient with moderate rheumatoid arthritis is being evaluated for biological therapy. Which of the following medications is classified as an anti-IL-6 receptor antagonist?
options: Infliximab
Rituximab
Anakinra
Abatacept
Tocilizumab
correctOption: Tocilizumab
optionExplanations: Infliximab is a biologic agent that inhibits tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), not IL-6.
Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody that targets CD20 on B-lymphocytes, leading to their depletion.
Anakinra is an interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist, belonging to the anti-IL-1 group rather than anti-IL-6.
Abatacept is a T-cell modulator that interferes with the costimulatory signals required for T-lymphocyte activation.
Tocilizumab is the specific biologic DMARD that targets and inhibits the activity of interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptors.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Anti-IL-6 drugs (tocilizumab) Upper respiratory tract infections, headache, hypertension, and elevated liver enzymes

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Tofacitinib is a newer agent used in the management of rheumatoid arthritis. Which of the following best describes its unique intracellular mechanism of action?
options: Irreversible inhibition of the cyclooxygenase-2 enzyme
Competitive inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase
Antagonism of the B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS)
Binding and neutralization of soluble TNF-alpha
Selective inhibition of the Janus kinase (JAK) pathway
correctOption: Selective inhibition of the Janus kinase (JAK) pathway
optionExplanations: Celecoxib is a selective COX-2 inhibitor; tofacitinib does not primarily target cyclooxygenase enzymes.
Methotrexate, not tofacitinib, acts by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase to interfere with immune cell division.
Belimumab is the agent that inhibits B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS), typically used in lupus management.
TNF-alpha inhibitors like etanercept or adalimumab bind to soluble TNF, whereas tofacitinib acts intracellularly.
Tofacitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that blocks intracellular signaling pathways critical for cytokine-mediated immune responses.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Tofacitinib (Janus kinase inhibitor) Infection, neutropenia, anemia, and increases in LDL and HDL

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of chronic gout, a physician chooses to prescribe febuxostat over allopurinol. What is a primary pharmacological contrast between these two xanthine oxidase inhibitors?
options: Febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor that exhibits greater selectivity for xanthine oxidase.
Allopurinol is more selective for xanthine oxidase than febuxostat.
Febuxostat increases renal urate excretion, whereas allopurinol decreases production.
Allopurinol acts by converting uric acid to allantoin, unlike febuxostat.
Febuxostat is a purine-based suicide inhibitor, while allopurinol is nonpurine.
correctOption: Febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor that exhibits greater selectivity for xanthine oxidase.
optionExplanations: Febuxostat is categorized as a selective, nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase, providing a pharmacological alternative to the purine-like allopurinol.
Febuxostat is actually more selective than allopurinol, as allopurinol can inhibit other enzymes in purine/pyrimidine metabolism.
Both drugs are xanthine oxidase inhibitors that reduce uric acid production; they are not uricosurics like probenecid.
Both drugs inhibit xanthine oxidase; neither converts uric acid to allantoin (that is the mechanism of pegloticase).
Allopurinol is the purine-based inhibitor, whereas febuxostat is specifically a nonpurine molecule.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): The newer drug febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase that is more selective than allopurinol and alloxanthine, which inhibit other enzymes involved in purine and pyrimidine metabolism.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 68-year-old male with a 15-year history of chronic gout presents with multiple large tophi and a serum urate level of 11.5 mg/dL. He has failed to achieve target levels despite maximum tolerated doses of both allopurinol and probenecid. Which of the following recombinant enzymes is indicated for this patient's refractory condition?
options: Canakinumab
Sulfinpyrazone
Auranofin
Leflunomide
Pegloticase
correctOption: Pegloticase
optionExplanations: Canakinumab is an IL-1 inhibitor and is not a recombinant enzyme used for long-term urate reduction.
Sulfinpyrazone is a uricosuric agent, which the patient has essentially failed already (similar to probenecid).
Auranofin is an oral gold compound used for RA, having no role in the management of chronic refractory tophaceous gout.
Leflunomide is a DMARD used for rheumatoid arthritis, not for the management of uric acid levels in gout.
Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase indicated specifically for chronic gout that is refractory to conventional xanthine oxidase inhibitors.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Pegloticase is approved for the treatment of refractory chronic gout.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Abatacept is a biological DMARD used for patients with inadequate response to methotrexate. What is its specific mechanism in modulating the immune response?
options: Lysis of B cells via complement-mediated cytotoxicity
Inhibition of pyrimidine synthesis via dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
Neutralization of the IL-6 cytokine in the synovial fluid
Interference with the activity of T lymphocytes by modulating costimulation
Blockade of the IL-1 receptor on macrophages
correctOption: Interference with the activity of T lymphocytes by modulating costimulation
optionExplanations: Rituximab is the agent that causes B-cell lysis; abatacept targets T-cell activation.
Leflunomide inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase to affect pyrimidine synthesis.
Tocilizumab is the agent that targets IL-6; abatacept does not interact directly with this cytokine.
Abatacept is a selective T-cell costimulation modulator that prevents the full activation of T-lymphocytes.
Anakinra is the drug that blocks the IL-1 receptor; abatacept's target is the T-lymphocyte signaling pathway.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Other drugs appear to interfere with the activity of T lymphocytes (eg, sulfasalazine, hydroxychloroquine, cyclosporine, leflunomide, mycophenolate mofetil, abatacept)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the standardized classification of drugs used for rheumatoid arthritis, which of the following is designated as a 'Conventional Synthetic' (cs) DMARD?
options: Methotrexate
Etanercept
Adalimumab
Certolizumab
Golimumab
correctOption: Methotrexate
optionExplanations: Methotrexate is the prototype conventional synthetic DMARD, distinguishing it from newer biological or targeted synthetic agents.
Etanercept is a biological (b) DMARD, specifically a TNF receptor fusion protein.
Adalimumab is a biological (b) DMARD, specifically a monoclonal antibody against TNF.
Certolizumab is a pegylated biological anti-TNF agent.
Golimumab is a biological anti-TNF agent.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 320 (Book Page): Methotrexate: Conventional synthetic (cs) cytotoxic to rapidly dividing immune cells due to inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient is being started on leflunomide for the management of rheumatoid arthritis. According to its known toxicity profile, which of the following risks must be prioritized during clinical monitoring?
options: Ocular toxicity and retinal damage
Teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity
Hyperuricemia and gout flares
Bone marrow suppression and peripheral neuritis
Cinchonism and heart block
correctOption: Teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity
optionExplanations: Ocular toxicity is the classic monitoring requirement for hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine.
Leflunomide is noted for being a significant teratogen and carrying a high risk of hepatotoxicity, requiring careful monitoring.
Leflunomide is used for RA and does not typically cause hyperuricemia or gout flares.
While many DMARDs cause marrow suppression, peripheral neuritis is more associated with allopurinol.
Cinchonism is associated with quinine/quinidine, not leflunomide.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Table 36–2: Leflunomide: Teratogen, hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal disturbance, skin reactions

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 55-year-old woman with a 2-year history of Rheumatoid Arthritis has been treated with optimal doses of Methotrexate. Despite this, she presents with persistent joint swelling, morning stiffness lasting 3 hours, and new erosions on hand X-rays. The physician decides to add a biological agent that binds to and neutralizes Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha. Which drug fits this description?
options: Abatacept
Sulfasalazine
Infliximab
Tofacitinib
Rituximab
correctOption: Infliximab
optionExplanations: Abatacept is a T-cell modulator that does not directly neutralize TNF-alpha.
Sulfasalazine is a conventional synthetic DMARD, not a biologic agent targeting TNF.
Infliximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to and inhibits TNF-alpha, suitable for patients failing MTX.
Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic JAK inhibitor, not a biologic monoclonal antibody.
Rituximab targets CD20 on B-cells and is not a direct TNF-alpha inhibitor.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Biologic agents that inhibit the action of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), including infliximab, adalimumab, and etanercept, have also shown efficacy in rheumatoid arthritis

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: What is the physiological mechanism by which pegloticase rapidly reduces serum urate levels in patients with chronic gout?
options: Blockade of the synthesis of purine precursors
Inhibition of the URAT1 transporter in the proximal tubule
Inhibition of microtubule polymerization in neutrophils
Oxidation of uric acid into the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
Irreversible suicide inhibition of xanthine oxidase
correctOption: Oxidation of uric acid into the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
optionExplanations: Methotrexate and other cytotoxic agents may interfere with purine synthesis, but pegloticase targets pre-existing uric acid.
This is the mechanism of uricosuric agents like probenecid.
This describes the mechanism of colchicine, which does not lower serum urate levels.
Pegloticase acts as a uricase enzyme, catalyzing the conversion of relatively insoluble uric acid into the highly soluble allantoin for renal clearance.
This describes allopurinol's mechanism, not pegloticase.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase. This enzyme, absent in humans, converts uric acid to the soluble allantoin, which can be eliminated by the kidney.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Which of the following medications is a recombinant human interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist used in the treatment of rheumatologic conditions?
options: Canakinumab
Rilonacept
Tocilizumab
Anakinra
Belimumab
correctOption: Anakinra
optionExplanations: Canakinumab is an anti-IL-1 monoclonal antibody, but anakinra is specifically the receptor antagonist mentioned as the prototype.
Rilonacept is a decoy receptor for IL-1, not the primary receptor antagonist described in the text as the human IL-1ra.
Tocilizumab is an IL-6 receptor antagonist.
Anakinra is the prototype recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist used to block the inflammatory effects of IL-1.
Belimumab inhibits B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS), not the IL-1 receptor.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page)-316: Biologic agents that inhibit... as has the recombinant human interleukin-1 receptor antagonist anakinra.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 44-year-old patient with severe, active rheumatoid arthritis who has failed to respond to methotrexate is being considered for a newer class of orally administered disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) that works by inhibiting Janus kinases (JAK). Which of the following drugs belongs to this specific subclass?
options: Tofacitinib
Abatacept
Tocilizumab
Rituximab
Anakinra
correctOption: Tofacitinib
optionExplanations: Tofacitinib is a newer DMARD that specifically inhibits the Janus kinase (JAK) signaling pathway, which is involved in the cytokine-mediated immune response in rheumatoid arthritis.
Abatacept is classified as a T-cell modulator, not a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. It acts by interfering with the costimulatory signal required for T-cell activation.
Tocilizumab is an anti-IL-6 receptor antibody used in RA, which prevents IL-6 from binding to its receptor, distinct from the intracellular JAK mechanism.
Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody that targets CD20 on B-lymphocytes, leading to their depletion, and does not involve kinase inhibition.
Anakinra is a recombinant human interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist, which acts by blocking the pro-inflammatory effects of IL-1 rather than inhibiting JAK.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": Table 36–2 Some Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs (DMARDs). ... Tofacitinib (Janus kinase inhibitor)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of acromegaly, a patient is prescribed pegvisomant to control the clinical manifestations of excessive growth hormone. Which of the following best describes the molecular mechanism of this agent?
options: Stimulation of somatostatin receptors on the pituitary adenoma
Inhibition of GHRH release from the hypothalamus
Degradation of circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1)
Binding to GH receptors to prevent functional receptor dimerization
Activation of dopamine D2 receptors to inhibit GH release
correctOption: Binding to GH receptors to prevent functional receptor dimerization
optionExplanations: Somatostatin analogs like octreotide stimulate somatostatin receptors (SSTR2 and SSTR5) to inhibit GH secretion; pegvisomant is a receptor antagonist.
Pegvisomant does not inhibit GHRH release; it acts peripherally at the target tissue receptors for GH.
Pegvisomant reduces the production of IGF-1 by blocking GH signaling, but it does not directly degrade IGF-1 itself.
Pegvisomant is a mutant GH analog that binds to GH receptors and prevents the conformational changes and dimerization necessary for signal transduction.
Dopamine D2 agonists like bromocriptine can inhibit GH release but are less effective than somatostatin analogs; pegvisomant works at the receptor level.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 324 (Book Page): Pegvisomant is a long-acting derivative of a mutant GH that is able to cross-link GH receptors but is incapable of inducing the conformational changes required for receptor activation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: When comparing the pharmacological profiles of xanthine oxidase inhibitors used in chronic gout, febuxostat is distinguished from allopurinol by which of the following characteristics?
options: It is converted to an active metabolite called oxypurinol
It is preferred over allopurinol during an acute gouty attack
It is a purine analog that acts as a suicide inhibitor
It primarily increases the renal excretion of uric acid
It is a nonpurine inhibitor that exhibits greater selectivity
correctOption: It is a nonpurine inhibitor that exhibits greater selectivity
optionExplanations: Allopurinol, not febuxostat, is converted by xanthine oxidase to the active metabolite oxypurinol (alloxanthine).
Neither drug should be started during an acute attack as they can precipitate flares; they are used for chronic management.
Allopurinol is the purine analog that acts as a suicide inhibitor; febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor.
Both drugs decrease production of uric acid; neither is a uricosuric agent (which would increase renal excretion).
Febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase and is more selective than allopurinol, as it does not inhibit other enzymes of purine/pyrimidine metabolism.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): The newer drug febuxostat is a nonpurine inhibitor of xanthine oxidase that is more selective than allopurinol and alloxanthine, which inhibit other enzymes involved in purine and pyrimidine metabolism.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 68-year-old male with a 15-year history of chronic tophaceous gout has failed to achieve target serum urate levels (<6 mg/dL) despite maximum tolerated doses of allopurinol and probenecid. His physical exam reveals multiple large tophi on his elbows and phalanges. He is started on an intravenous therapy that converts uric acid to a highly soluble metabolite. Which of the following describes the mechanism of the most appropriate next-line agent?
options: Antagonism of Interleukin-1 receptors
Recombinant uricase converting urate to allantoin
Competitive inhibition of the URAT1 transporter
Irreversible inhibition of xanthine oxidase
Inhibition of microtubule assembly in leukocytes
correctOption: Recombinant uricase converting urate to allantoin
optionExplanations: IL-1 antagonism (e.g., anakinra) addresses the inflammation of gout but does not lower serum urate levels or resolve tophi.
Pegloticase is a recombinant uricase used for refractory chronic gout; it converts uric acid into allantoin, which is much more soluble and easily excreted.
Competitive inhibition of renal reabsorption (URAT1) is the mechanism of uricosurics like probenecid, which this patient has already failed.
Irreversible inhibition of xanthine oxidase is the mechanism of allopurinol, which the patient has already failed.
Inhibition of microtubule assembly is the mechanism of colchicine, which is used for acute flares or prophylaxis, not for lowering total body urate burden in refractory disease.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase. This enzyme, absent in humans, converts uric acid to the soluble allantoin, which can be eliminated by the kidney.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 62-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis and comorbid Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is being evaluated for new DMARD therapy. The physician decides to exercise caution because which of the following agents is specifically associated with an increased risk of COPD exacerbations?
options: Abatacept
Leflunomide
Methotrexate
Sulfasalazine
Hydroxychloroquine
correctOption: Abatacept
optionExplanations: Abatacept, a T-cell modulator, is associated with toxicities including infection and, notably, the exacerbation of COPD in patients with preexisting lung disease.
Leflunomide is known for hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity, but not specifically COPD exacerbations.
Methotrexate toxicity includes nausea, mucosal ulcers, and hepatotoxicity, but it is not specifically linked to COPD exacerbation in the provided text.
Sulfasalazine commonly causes rash, GI disturbance, and leukopenia, but not specific COPD flares.
Hydroxychloroquine's major unique toxicities include ocular damage and myopathy, rather than pulmonary exacerbations.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": Table 36–2 Some Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs (DMARDs). ... Abatacept (T-cell modulator) ... Infection, exacerbation of COPD

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A physician is selecting an analgesic for a postoperative patient and chooses ketorolac because of its unique availability among nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Which property of ketorolac is being utilized?
options: It lacks the renal toxicities associated with other NSAIDs
It is available in a parenteral formulation
It selectively inhibits COX-2 and spares COX-1
It is the only NSAID safe for use in children with viral infections
It is the only NSAID that does not affect bleeding time
correctOption: It is available in a parenteral formulation
optionExplanations: Ketorolac carries a significant risk of renal and GI damage, and its use is typically restricted to 72 hours for this reason.
Ketorolac is notable because it is the only NSAID available in a parenteral (injectable) formulation, making it useful for systemic analgesia in hospital settings.
Ketorolac is a nonselective NSAID, meaning it inhibits both COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes.
Acetaminophen, not ketorolac, is the preferred substitute for aspirin in children with viral infections to avoid Reye's syndrome.
Ketorolac, like other nonselective NSAIDs, does prolong bleeding time and has typical NSAID properties.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 314 (Book Page): It is the only NSAID available in a parenteral formulation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A child with growth failure due to a severe deficiency of Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1) is prescribed mecasermin. The parents are instructed to ensure the child consumes a snack shortly before each injection to mitigate which primary adverse effect?
options: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
Hypoglycemia
Peripheral edema
Hyperglycemia
Pseudotumor cerebri
correctOption: Hypoglycemia
optionExplanations: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is a risk with Somatropin therapy in children with growth failure.
Mecasermin, being recombinant IGF-1, has significant insulin-like activity and can cause profound hypoglycemia; eating before administration is a critical safety measure.
Edema can occur with Somatropin use, especially in adults, but it is not the acute toxicity managed by pre-dose snacking in mecasermin patients.
Hyperglycemia is a potential adverse effect of Somatropin (GH), but mecasermin (IGF-1) has insulin-like effects and causes the opposite.
Pseudotumor cerebri is a rare but serious adverse effect associated with Growth Hormone (Somatropin) therapy, not specifically emphasized for mecasermin.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 323 (Book Page): Mecasermin, recombinant human IGF-1... Its most important toxicity is hypoglycemia, which can be prevented by consumption of a snack or meal shortly before mecasermin administration.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 55-year-old woman with a 10-year history of rheumatoid arthritis presents for a follow-up. She has been taking a conventional DMARD for several years. She mentions new-found difficulty in reading and a 'blurring' of her central vision. Funduscopic examination reveals pigmentary changes in the macula. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for these findings?
options: Leflunomide
Chloroquine
Cyclosporine
Methotrexate
Sulfasalazine
correctOption: Chloroquine
optionExplanations: Leflunomide is primarily associated with hepatotoxicity and GI upset; it is not known for causing retinal pigmentary changes.
Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are DMARDs that can cause cumulative ocular toxicity, specifically retinal damage that may present as blurred vision and maculopathy.
Cyclosporine is primarily nephrotoxic and can cause hypertension, but it does not cause the specific macular pigmentary changes seen with antimalarials.
Methotrexate toxicities are primarily hematologic, hepatic, and mucosal; it does not typically cause pigmentary retinopathy.
Sulfasalazine toxicities include rash, headache, and leukopenia, but not the ocular changes described.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": Table 36–2 Some Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs (DMARDs). ... Hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine ... ocular toxicity

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Octreotide and lanreotide are synthetic analogs used to treat acromegaly and certain endocrine tumors. These agents mimic the physiological inhibitory action of somatostatin on which set of hormones?
options: ACTH, TSH, and GH
GH, Insulin, and Glucagon
IGF-1, IGF-2, and Somatropin
GH, LH, and FSH
Prolactin, Oxytocin, and ADH
correctOption: GH, Insulin, and Glucagon
optionExplanations: ACTH and TSH have their own hypothalamic regulators (CRH and TRH); somatostatin does not serve as their primary inhibitory regulator.
Somatostatin is a potent universal inhibitor that reduces the secretion of Growth Hormone (GH), insulin, glucagon, and gastrin.
Somatropin is GH; IGF-1 and IGF-2 are growth factors produced in response to GH, but they are not the direct targets of somatostatin inhibition.
While somatostatin inhibits GH, the gonadotropins (LH/FSH) are primarily regulated by GnRH, not somatostatin.
Prolactin is regulated by dopamine; oxytocin and ADH are posterior pituitary hormones not primarily regulated by somatostatin.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 324 (Book Page): Somatostatin, a 14-amino-acid peptide, inhibits the release of GH, glucagon, insulin, and gastrin.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient with moderate rheumatoid arthritis is starting a biologic agent that acts specifically as a recombinant interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist. Which drug is being prescribed?
options: Golimumab
Infliximab
Etanercept
Anakinra
Adalimumab
correctOption: Anakinra
optionExplanations: Golimumab is another anti-TNF-alpha monoclonal antibody used in the treatment of RA.
Infliximab is a monoclonal antibody against TNF-alpha, not an IL-1 receptor antagonist.
Etanercept is a soluble fusion protein that binds to and inactivates TNF-alpha, not IL-1.
Anakinra is the specific biologic DMARD that functions as a recombinant human interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist.
Adalimumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting TNF-alpha.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 316 (Book Page): recombinant human interleukin-1 receptor antagonist anakinra.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 34-year-old male recently diagnosed with lepromatous leprosy is initiated on multidrug therapy (MDT). The primary drug in his regimen acts by inhibiting dihydropteroate synthase, thereby preventing the synthesis of folic acid. Which of the following drugs is being described?
options: Clofazimine
Rifampin
Dapsone
Ethionamide
Minocycline
correctOption: Dapsone
optionExplanations: Clofazimine's mechanism is not fully understood but likely involves binding to DNA and generating cytotoxic oxygen radicals, rather than folate inhibition.
Rifampin acts by binding to the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, inhibiting RNA synthesis, not folate synthesis.

Dapsone is a sulfone structurally related to sulfonamides. It competitively inhibits the enzyme dihydropteroate synthase, which prevents the incorporation of PABA into dihydrofolic acid, a mechanism shared with sulfonamide antimicrobials mentioned in the text for their cross-allergenicity.
Ethionamide inhibits the synthesis of mycolic acids, similar to isoniazid, and is used as a second-line agent in leprosy.
Minocycline is a tetracycline that inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit; it is used as an alternative agent in leprosy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Because they are sulfonamides, the uricosuric drugs may share allergenicity with other classes of sulfonamide drugs (diuretics, antimicrobials, oral hypoglycemic drugs).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of multibacillary leprosy, the WHO-recommended multidrug therapy (MDT) includes a drug that is uniquely bactericidal and acts by inhibiting bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase. What is the standard adult monthly supervised dose of this agent?
options: 50 mg
100 mg
600 mg
300 mg
correctOption: 600 mg
optionExplanations: 50 mg is the daily dose of clofazimine used in the multibacillary regimen, not rifampin.
100 mg is the daily dose for dapsone in the MDT regimen, not the monthly supervised rifampin dose.
1000 mg is an excessive dose for rifampin and exceeds the standard supervised dose used in leprosy management.
Rifampin is highly bactericidal against M. leprae. In the WHO MDT regimen for leprosy, it is administered as a single monthly supervised dose of 600 mg.
300 mg is used in some pediatric regimens or as a daily dose in other conditions, but not as the supervised monthly dose in adult leprosy MDT.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Rifampin is the primary bactericidal agent in MDT regimens]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 42-year-old patient with leprosy is undergoing treatment and develops a dark reddish-brown discoloration of the skin and conjunctiva. This effect is a known side effect of a drug that also possesses anti-inflammatory properties used to manage Type 2 leprosy reactions. What is the mechanism of this drug?
options: Inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
Inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase
Antagonism of PABA for folate synthesis
Binding to DNA and generation of oxygen radicals
Inhibition of microtubule assembly
correctOption: Binding to DNA and generation of oxygen radicals
optionExplanations: This is the mechanism of rifampin, which does not cause the characteristic reddish-brown skin discoloration associated with leprosy treatment.
This is the specific enzyme targeted by dapsone, which is a bacteriostatic agent and does not cause skin pigmentation.
This is the mechanism of dapsone and sulfonamides, which are more commonly associated with hemolytic anemia or rashes rather than deep skin pigmentation.

Clofazimine is a phenazine dye that binds to bacterial DNA, inhibiting its template function. It also increases the production of reactive oxygen species in cells, contributing to its bactericidal and anti-inflammatory actions. Skin discoloration is a hallmark toxicity.
This is the mechanism of colchicine (Page 316), used in gout, not a primary leprosy drug.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Clofazimine causes skin discoloration and is used for its anti-inflammatory effects]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 29-year-old male with multibacillary leprosy presents with sudden onset of painful erythematous skin nodules, fever, and arthralgia, consistent with Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL). Which medication, historically known for its teratogenicity, is highly effective for this Type 2 reaction?
options: Thalidomide
Methotrexate
Prednisolone
Aspirin
Cyclosporine
correctOption: Thalidomide
optionExplanations: Thalidomide is highly effective for managing Type 2 lepra reactions (ENL). Due to its severe teratogenicity, its use is strictly regulated, but it remains a mainstay for severe ENL in males and non-pregnant females.
Methotrexate is a DMARD used for rheumatoid arthritis (Page 315) and is not a primary treatment for lepra reactions.
Prednisolone is used for lepra reactions but is not the drug specifically highlighted for its historical teratogenicity in this context.
Aspirin is an NSAID used for mild pain (Page 314) but lacks the specific immunomodulatory efficacy required for severe ENL.
Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressant used in transplantation or severe RA (Page 315) but is not the first-line historical choice for ENL compared to thalidomide.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Thalidomide is indicated for Type 2 reactions/ENL]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: Which of the following drugs used in leprosy is classified as a phenazine dye and acts primarily as a bacteriostatic agent against Mycobacterium leprae, but also serves as a component of the MDT regimen to prevent resistance?
options: Clofazimine
Dapsone
Ofloxacin
Rifampin
Clarithromycin
correctOption: Clofazimine
optionExplanations: Clofazimine is a phenazine dye used in the treatment of multibacillary leprosy. It is weakly bactericidal to M. leprae and is included in MDT regimens to prevent the emergence of dapsone resistance.
Dapsone is a sulfone, not a dye. While it is bacteriostatic and used in MDT, it belongs to the sulfonamide-related class.
Ofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used as an alternative agent in leprosy, acting via DNA gyrase inhibition.
Rifampin is a bactericidal rifamycin derivative, not a phenazine dye.
Clarithromycin is a macrolide used as an alternative agent, acting via the 50S ribosomal subunit.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Clofazimine is a phenazine dye]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
coreConcept: WHO Leprosy Classification and MDT Duration
statement: The WHO classification of leprosy determines the duration and complexity of the drug regimen. A patient with three skin lesions and no bacilli found on a skin smear is classified as having which form of the disease, and what is the recommended treatment duration?
options: Borderline; 24 months
Paucibacillary; 6 months
Paucibacillary; 12 months
Multibacillary; 12 months
Multibacillary; 6 months
correctOption: Paucibacillary; 6 months
optionExplanations: Borderline is a clinical sub-classification, but for treatment purposes, patients are simplified into PB or MB by the WHO.
Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy is defined by 1-5 skin lesions and negative smears. The WHO MDT for PB involves rifampin and dapsone for 6 months.
While the patient is PB, the 12-month duration is reserved for the MB form.
Multibacillary (MB) leprosy involves more than 5 lesions or positive smears and requires a 12-month triple-drug regimen (Rifampin, Dapsone, Clofazimine).
MB leprosy requires a minimum of 12 months, not 6 months, to ensure eradication of the higher bacterial load.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Paucibacillary leprosy requires 6 months of MDT]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A leprosy patient on dapsone therapy presents with fatigue and jaundice. Laboratory tests reveal a significant drop in hemoglobin and the presence of Heinz bodies. This patient most likely has a deficiency in which of the following?
options: Iron
Xanthine oxidase
Folate
Vitamin B12
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD)
correctOption: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD)
optionExplanations: Iron deficiency causes microcytic hypochromic anemia, which is distinct from the hemolytic process described.
Xanthine oxidase is involved in purine metabolism and gout (Page 317) but is not related to the hemolytic side effects of dapsone.
While dapsone interferes with folate synthesis in bacteria, it does not typically cause acute hemolysis via human folate deficiency.
Vitamin B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia, not the acute hemolytic anemia and Heinz bodies seen with oxidative drug triggers.
Dapsone, as a sulfone/oxidant drug, can cause acute hemolytic anemia in patients with G6PD deficiency. This is a critical contraindication or precaution in leprosy treatment.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Allopurinol is converted to oxypurinol... it inhibits the metabolism of mercaptopurine... [Sulfonamide/Sulfone similarity implies oxidative stress risk]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient with leprosy who has failed standard MDT due to rifampin resistance requires an alternative regimen. Which of the following is a second-line agent that acts by inhibiting protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit?
options: Ethionamide
Amoxicillin
Ofloxacin
Minocycline
Clarithromycin
correctOption: Minocycline
optionExplanations: Ethionamide is a thioamide that inhibits mycolic acid synthesis, not protein synthesis via ribosomes.
Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam that inhibits cell wall synthesis and is not typically used for leprosy treatment.
Ofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that inhibits DNA gyrase, not the 30S ribosome.
Minocycline is a tetracycline antibiotic that inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit. It has significant activity against M. leprae and is used in alternative regimens.
Clarithromycin is a macrolide that inhibits the 50S ribosomal subunit, not the 30S.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Minocycline is an alternative agent]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: The 'Dapsone Syndrome' is a severe hypersensitivity reaction that can occur within the first few weeks of leprosy treatment. Which of the following clinical triads best describes this potentially fatal condition?
options: Alopecia, neuropathy, and hypertension
Rash, hematuria, and joint pain
Diarrhea, dermatitis, and dementia
Tinnitus, hyperventilation, and metabolic acidosis
Fever, jaundice, and eosinophilia
correctOption: Fever, jaundice, and eosinophilia
optionExplanations: These symptoms are not associated with the acute hypersensitivity reaction caused by dapsone.
This may describe Henoch-Schönlein purpura or certain vasculitides, but not the specific Dapsone Syndrome.
This '3 Ds' triad describes Pellagra (Niacin deficiency), not a drug reaction.
This triad is characteristic of salicylate (aspirin) toxicity (Page 314), not dapsone.

Dapsone Hypersensitivity Syndrome (or 'Sulfone Syndrome') is characterized by fever, malaise, exfoliative dermatitis, jaundice (with hepatic dysfunction), and lymphadenopathy. It can be fatal if the drug is not discontinued.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Dapsone Syndrome features]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
coreConcept: Rationale for Multidrug Therapy (MDT) in Leprosy
statement: In the treatment of leprosy, what is the primary pharmacological reason for combining dapsone with clofazimine and rifampin in multibacillary patients?
options: To increase the oral bioavailability of rifampin
To reduce the incidence of skin discoloration from clofazimine
To decrease the renal clearance of dapsone
To delay or prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains
To provide synergistic inhibition of folate synthesis
correctOption: To delay or prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains
optionExplanations: The drugs do not significantly interact to increase the bioavailability of rifampin.
Combining the drugs does not reduce clofazimine's skin side effects; in fact, it may make the overall regimen more difficult to tolerate.
The combination is not designed to alter the renal clearance of the drugs; its purpose is antimicrobial efficacy and resistance prevention.

Multidrug therapy (MDT) is essential in leprosy to prevent the development of resistance to individual agents, particularly dapsone, which was used as monotherapy for decades leading to widespread resistance.
The drugs have distinct mechanisms (RNA polymerase, DNA binding, and folate synthesis); they do not all target folate synthesis.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology": [Topic-Specific Demand: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy - Rationale for MDT]

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 34-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus is evaluated for the addition of a biologic agent that specifically targets the B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) to reduce disease activity. In the pharmacological classification of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), which of the following agents is identified for this specific role?
options: Anakinra
Abatacept
Tocilizumab
Belimumab
Tofacitinib
correctOption: Belimumab
optionExplanations: Anakinra is a recombinant human interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist, used primarily in rheumatoid arthritis, not for BLyS inhibition.
Abatacept is classified as a T-cell modulator, not a B-lymphocyte stimulator inhibitor; it works by interfering with the co-stimulatory signal required for T-cell activation.
Tocilizumab is an anti-IL-6 receptor antibody used in rheumatoid arthritis and is not involved in the inhibition of the BLyS pathway.
Belimumab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS), thereby reducing the survival of B cells; it is specifically indicated for systemic lupus erythematosus.
Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, which acts on intracellular signaling pathways rather than extracellular B-lymphocyte stimulators.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 315 (Book Page): Belimumab (inhibits B-lymphocyte stimulator [BLyS]) Systemic lupus erythematosus Nausea, diarrhea, and respiratory tract infection

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 45-year-old male with a history of nasal polyps and chronic rhinosinusitis experiences a sudden onset of bronchospasm and wheezing after taking a standard dose of aspirin for a headache. Which of the following pathophysiological mechanisms best explains this reaction?
options: Activation of the classic complement pathway by salicylate crystals
IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity to the salicylate molecule
Direct stimulation of histamine release from mast cells
Increased synthesis of leukotrienes due to cyclooxygenase inhibition
Irreversible blockade of endothelial prostacyclin receptors
correctOption: Increased synthesis of leukotrienes due to cyclooxygenase inhibition
optionExplanations: Salicylate reactions are typically pharmacological (pseudoallergic) rather than being driven by type II or type III hypersensitivity involving crystal-mediated complement activation.
Aspirin hypersensitivity is generally not an IgE-mediated allergy; it is a biochemical intolerance related to the inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis and subsequent leukotriene imbalance.
While mast cell degranulation can cause asthma, aspirin-induced asthma is specifically linked to the metabolic shunting of arachidonic acid towards the lipoxygenase pathway.

Aspirin inhibits the cyclooxygenase (COX) pathway, which diverts arachidonic acid metabolism toward the lipoxygenase pathway, leading to an overproduction of pro-inflammatory and bronchoconstrictive leukotrienes.
Aspirin does irreversibly inhibit COX-1 and COX-2, but the asthma reaction is caused by the shift to leukotriene synthesis, not the direct blockade of prostacyclin receptors.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 314 (Book Page): When prostaglandin synthesis is inhibited by even small doses of aspirin, persons with aspirin hypersensitivity (especially associated with nasal polyps) can experience asthma from the increased synthesis of leukotrienes.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A patient with chronic refractory gout is treated with pegloticase. Which of the following biochemical transformations describes the mechanism by which this drug facilitates the elimination of uric acid?
options: Competitive inhibition of the URAT1 transporter in the proximal tubule
Degradation of macrophage microtubules to prevent phagocytosis
Irreversible inhibition of the suicide-type xanthine oxidase enzyme
Oxidation of hypoxanthine to the more soluble xanthine
Conversion of uric acid to the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
correctOption: Conversion of uric acid to the highly soluble metabolite allantoin
optionExplanations: Competitive inhibition of uric acid reabsorption transporters is the mechanism of uricosuric agents like probenecid, not uricase enzymes.
Inhibition of microtubule assembly is the mechanism of action for colchicine, which reduces the inflammatory response rather than altering uric acid chemistry.
Suicide inhibition of xanthine oxidase is the mechanism of alloxanthine (the metabolite of allopurinol), not pegloticase.
The oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine is a natural step in purine metabolism catalyzed by xanthine oxidase, which xanthine oxidase inhibitors actually block.
Pegloticase is a recombinant uricase that breaks down uric acid—which is poorly soluble—into allantoin, a much more soluble substance that is easily excreted by the kidneys.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 317 (Book Page): Pegloticase is a recombinant mammalian uricase. This enzyme, absent in humans, converts uric acid to the soluble allantoin, which can be eliminated by the kidney.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: A 50-year-old male with acromegaly due to a pituitary adenoma has failed to achieve adequate reduction in insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels despite maximal therapy with octreotide. The medical team decides to switch to pegvisomant. Which of the following describes the unique pharmacological advantage of pegvisomant in this clinical scenario?
options: It acts as a long-acting dopamine D2 receptor agonist to shrink the tumor
It prevents growth hormone from inducing receptor conformational changes despite binding
It increases the sensitivity of the liver to endogenous somatostatin-14
It stimulates the production of IGF-binding protein-3 to sequester free IGF-1
It provides more potent inhibition of the release of growth hormone from the pituitary
correctOption: It prevents growth hormone from inducing receptor conformational changes despite binding
optionExplanations: Dopamine agonists like bromocriptine have low efficacy in acromegaly compared to GH-specific agents and are not the mechanism for pegvisomant.

Pegvisomant is a mutated GH molecule that can bind to the GH receptor and even cause dimerization (cross-linking), but it is engineered to prevent the necessary conformational change for signal transduction.
Pegvisomant does not interact with the somatostatin system; it works directly on the growth hormone receptor.
While IGFBP-3 levels can change during therapy, pegvisomant's primary and defining mechanism is direct growth hormone receptor antagonism.
Pegvisomant does not inhibit the release of growth hormone; it is a receptor antagonist. Octreotide is the drug that inhibits release.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 324 (Book Page): Pegvisomant is a long-acting derivative of a mutant GH that is able to cross-link GH receptors but is incapable of inducing the conformational changes required for receptor activation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
statement: In the management of rheumatoid arthritis, certain slow-acting antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) target specific cellular components of the immune system. Which of the following DMARDs is traditionally believed to exert its anti-inflammatory effect primarily by interfering with the activity of macrophages?
options: Gold compounds
Sulfasalazine
Leflunomide
Tofacitinib
Rituximab
correctOption: Gold compounds
optionExplanations: Gold compounds, although rarely used now, are recognized in pharmacology for their ability to interfere with the functional activity of macrophages in the inflammatory process.
Sulfasalazine is grouped with agents that appear to interfere with T lymphocyte activity in the context of rheumatoid arthritis.
Leflunomide is classified in the text as a drug that primarily interferes with the activity of T lymphocytes.
